description: Curated festival rules covering lunar tithi observances and solar calendar transitions (Sankranti and Solar New Years). Verify each rule against reliable published sources and regional Panchang conventions before treating it as authoritative.

festivals.name: Diwali
festivals.notes: The observance and date-selection conventions may vary by region and calendar tradition.

festivals.name: Holi
festivals.notes: Regional observance conventions and local calendars should be checked.

festivals.name: Rama Navami
festivals.notes: The applicable Panchang and local observance convention must be confirmed.

festivals.name: Krishna Janmashtami
festivals.notes: Regional calendars and observance conventions may differ; verify the applicable rule.

festivals.name: Makar Sankranti
festivals.notes: Sun enters sidereal Makara (Capricorn). In traditional observance, if ingress occurs after sunset, the festival is observed on the following day. Marks the sacred Punya Kala window.

festivals.name: Pongal
festivals.notes: Celebrated on the first day of the Tamil solar month Thai, synchronized with the Sun's Makara transit. Dedicated to Surya and agricultural bounty.

festivals.name: Mesha Sankranti
festivals.notes: Sun enters sidereal Mesha (Aries), the zero point of the Nirayana zodiac. Forms the astronomical basis for regional solar new year festivals across India.

festivals.name: Puthandu
festivals.notes: First day of Chithirai month. If Mesha Sankranti occurs before sunset, that civil day is Chithirai 1; otherwise the next day.

festivals.name: Vishu
festivals.notes: Kerala astronomical new year. Historically connected to the vernal equinox (Vishuva) when day and night were equal. Celebrated with Vishukkani.

festivals.name: Poila Boishakh
festivals.notes: First day of Boishakh. Determined by the transit of Sun into Mesha using the Panjika Danda rule (if transit occurs before midnight/sunset).
festivals.source: Surya Siddhanta & Drik Siddhanta Bengali Panjika

festivals.name: Pana Sankranti
festivals.notes: Odia solar New Year celebrating the arrival of the spring/summer solar cycle with sweet Bela Pana offerings.

festivals.name: Baisakhi
festivals.notes: Solar harvest festival marking the Sun's ingress into Mesha. Also commemorates the formation of Khalsa Panth in 1699 CE.

festivals.name: Karka Sankranti
festivals.notes: Sun enters sidereal Karka (Cancer), marking the traditional commencement of Dakshinayana (southward movement of the Sun).

festivals.name: Chhath Puja
festivals.notes: Rigvedic solar thanksgiving ritual. Devotees offer Arghya to setting and rising Sun along riverbanks, honoring the solar life-force.

festivals.name: Ratha Saptami
festivals.notes: Celebrates Surya turning his seven-horse chariot (representing the 7 rays/days) towards the north-east, heralding warmer spring days.
